chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) sent someone to Bishr ibn Utarid al-Tameemi regarding a speech that reached him. So the messenger of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) passed by him among the Banu Asad and seized him. So Nu'aym ibn Dajaja al-Asadi stood up to him and released him.

So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) sent someone to him, so they brought him to him, and he (peace be upon him) ordered that he be whipped. So Nu'aym said to him (peace be upon him): 'By Allah, staying with you is a disgrace, and separation from you is infidelity.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'When I heard that from you, I said to you, O Nu'aym, we have pardoned you.'
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'Repel evil by what is best.'

As for your saying, 'Staying with you is a disgrace,' that is an evil you have acquired; and as for your saying, 'Separation from you is infidelity,' that is a good deed you have acquired. So this (the good) compensates for this (the evil).
Then he ordered that he be released.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ: Repel evil by what is best (Quranic principle)
key_terms.بِشْرُ بْنُ عُطَارِدٍ: Bishr ibn Utarid, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.نُعَيْمُ بْنُ دَجَاجَةَ: Nu'aym ibn Dajaja, known for his loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: How did Amir al-Mu'minin interpret Nu'aym's statement about disgrace and infidelity in light of the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) strategic use of *sabr* (patience) and *ihsan* (excellence) to neutralize political opposition, specifically Nu'aym ibn Dajaja, by transforming a potentially divisive statement into a basis for pardon. The Imam’s interpretation of Nu'aym’s paradoxical remark—where 'disgrace' was treated as a minor evil and 'infidelity' as a good deed of loyalty—demonstrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual exegesis (*ta'wil*) in applying Quranic principles to governance. This incident highlights the practical application of Surah Fussilat 41:34, showing how diplomatic grace can secure allegiance without force.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> sent someone to Bishr Bin Utaradi Al-Tameemy regarding a speech which reached him<sup>asws</sup>. So the messenger of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> passed by him among the Clan of Asad and seized him. So Nuaym Bin Dajaja Al-Asady stood up to him and had him released.

So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> sent someone to him, so he came up with him, and he<sup>asws</sup> ordered for him to be whipped. So Nuaym said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the staying with you<sup>asws</sup> is a disgrace, and in separation from you<sup>asws</sup> is infidelity’.
So when he<sup>asws</sup> heard that from him, he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘O Nuaym! We<sup>asws</sup> have excused you,
for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [23:96] Repel evil by what is best.

As for your words that, ‘Staying with you<sup>asws</sup> is disgrace’, so it is an evil which you have attained; and as for your words, ‘In separation from you<sup>asws</sup> is infidelity’, so it is a good deed which you have attained. So this here (compensates) for this’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that he be released from it’.
